homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym: card 1 is the database, cards 2 and 3 are other publishers of union membership data (BLS, EPI), distinct entities on the same subject. 'Unionstats' and 'Union Membership, Coverage, and Earnings from the CPS' are names of the entity (B4, B5; census aka). In the archive, 'CPS' is also the archive's own signature metric in #302 (the Authorial Signature Diagnostic Framework), a homonym of the acronym, read and not admitted.
distinct_entities: the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Union Members Summary, the official annual release from the CPS (B2; Wikipedia's 2025 state table, B6 F25)
the Economic Policy Institute's union membership data and its tables (B3)
Union Density Estimates by State, 1964–2015 (Hirsch, Macpherson and Vroman, 2016; Georgia State University, unionstats.gsu.edu), listed beneath the database on Wikipedia (B6 F24)
the 2003 note in the ILR Review, 56(2), 349–354, by Hirsch and Macpherson, describing the database (B6 F26)
the Current Population Survey, the household survey the estimates are compiled from (B4)
the operators: Barry Hirsch, David Macpherson, William Even (B4, B5; Wikipedia, Barry Hirsch)
'CPS' in #302, the archive's signature metric (not admitted)

captures.description: THE DATABASE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The Union Membership and Coverage Database is an annual internet data resource created and maintained by economists Barry Hirsch, David Macpherson, and William Even.' Source material; timeline; latest data; a request for the user's role. Three cards: the database, BLS, EPI.

atoms.evidence: Union Membership and Coverage Database from the CPS (Unionstats.com)
is an annual internet data resource created and maintained by economists Barry Hirsch, David Macpherson, and William Even.
Compiles private- and public-sector labor union membership, coverage, and density estimates from the monthly household Current Population Survey (CPS)
